raw: 2.1 U.S. Intelligence Community: 18 Agencies, Authorities, and Relationships[^6]
teaching_note: The public IC overview inspected for this curriculum on 6 November 2026 lists 18 elements or organizations, not 18 interchangeable standalone agencies [@official_intelligence_gov_how_ic_works]. Distinguish ODNI coordination/integration, CIA foreign-intelligence work, NSA signals-intelligence responsibilities, and departmental or military elements serving their respective remits; this is a role orientation, not a complete or current authorization chart. **Completed synthetic handoff:** a supplied public weather bulletin and fictional port-status record go from an analyst to a coordinating review role, then to the logistics decision-owner; a release reviewer receives only the source/caveat summary needed to approve classroom distribution. When the status record's permission field is missing, the reviewer holds that record and releases only the independently permitted bulletin summary; the analyst must not treat coordination, collection, release, and policy decision as one power.
title: U.S. Intelligence Community: Elements, Functions, and Responsibility

raw: 2.2 Soviet/Russian Architecture: Cheka → GPU → NKVD → MGB → KGB → SVR/FSB/GRU
teaching_note: The inherited arrow list is a historical prompt, not an accurate single chain of equivalent institutions or a certified current organization chart. Distinguish political-security institutions, foreign intelligence, domestic security, and military intelligence; do not present GRU military intelligence as simply another successor branch of the KGB. The supplied ICD citations concern U.S. analytic standards and do not establish Soviet/Russian institutional chronology, present remits, or accountability. A comparison card must date each named body and leave unsupported succession, oversight, and present authority cells unknown rather than infer them from a familiar acronym.
title: Soviet and Russian Institutions: Historical Lineage and Comparison Limits

raw: 2.3 British Architecture: MI5, MI6/SIS, GCHQ, DI, JIC[^7]
teaching_note: The useful functional contrast is domestic security (MI5), foreign intelligence (SIS/MI6), signals/cyber work (GCHQ), defence intelligence (DI), and coordinated assessment (JIC); an assessment body is not interchangeable with a collection service. Treat these as introductory role labels whose precise legal remits and oversight arrangements require dated authoritative records. The inherited historical British source does not certify a 2026 reporting chain or current sharing permission. Diagnostic answer: a JIC-related assessment label alone does not show who collected the underlying information or who may release it; preserve those as separate provenance and authority questions.
title: British Intelligence: Security, Foreign Intelligence, Defence, and Assessment Roles

raw: 2.4 Israeli Architecture: Mossad, Shin Bet, Unit 8200, LAKAM[^8]
teaching_note: Distinguish the introductory categories of foreign intelligence (Mossad), internal security (Shin Bet), and military signals intelligence (Unit 8200), without treating them as equivalent bodies or asserting a complete chain of authority. LAKAM belongs in explicitly historical discussion, not an undated list of assumed current institutions. The inherited Mossad overview does not support the entire Israeli architecture, detailed remits, or present oversight; those cells remain unverified pending dated primary records. A source discussing one organization cannot silently validate claims about all organizations named beside it.
title: Israeli Institutions: Role Labels and Historical Scope

raw: 2.5 Chinese Architecture: MSS, PLA-SSF, United Front Work Department, APT Groups[^9]
teaching_note: The inherited MERICS source is November 2023 analysis: PLA Strategic Support Force (PLA-SSF) is explicitly pre-April-2024-reorganization historical context, not an assumed current institution. This source cannot certify a 2026 PLA organization chart, so present structure and exact successor remits remain outside its supported scope. State-security, military, and party bodies are different institutional categories; an APT label is an analytic attribution label, not itself proof of formal membership, command, capability, or legal responsibility. A correct comparison records the date and claimed relationship separately and withholds a current or actor-attribution conclusion where primary evidence is absent.
title: Chinese Institutions: Historical PLA-SSF Context and Attribution Limits

raw: 2.6 Five Eyes and Allied Intelligence Sharing: BRUSA to UKUSA[^10][^11]
teaching_note: Historical BRUSA/UKUSA records can establish an agreement's wording and institutional setting at a stated date; they do not by themselves establish every contemporary Five Eyes practice. Sharing arrangements coordinate partners with distinct domestic authorities rather than create one borderless agency or a blanket right to redistribute material. In the synthetic port handoff, an allied-source tag is not release permission: the recipient needs the supplied originator caveat and permitted audience, and an unknown field triggers a hold. Separate agreement date, archival release date, record completeness, and the present claim being made.
title: BRUSA, UKUSA, and Allied Sharing: History versus Permission

raw: 2.7 Non-State Intelligence Actors: Terrorist, Criminal, PMC[^12]
teaching_note: Non-state actors may gather, interpret, and use information, but organizational labels such as criminal, terrorist, or private military company do not establish a particular person's conduct, intent, or legal status. Compare purpose, resources, accountability, and access only to the extent documented in a supplied historical or synthetic case. A researcher's use of public information is not evidence of hostile collection, and similarity of technique is not evidence of shared sponsorship. The inherited source supplies contextual discussion, not a license to investigate real people or a validated attribution test.
title: Non-State Intelligence Activity: Categories without Person-Level Attribution

raw: 2.8 Fusion Centers, JITFs, and Inter-Agency Coordination
teaching_note: The DHS overview, last updated 17 October 2022, describes US fusion centers as state-owned and operated information-sharing and analysis centers [@ageint313]. That description does not define every task-force model or transfer participants' statutory powers. The inherited acronym JITF is not expanded by its cited evidence and must not silently be read as JTTF, a particular Joint Intelligence Task Force, or another organization. Leave the intended JITF model unresolved until a dated charter supplies its full name, membership, scope, and accountable lead. In a fictional handoff, the useful fields are sending role, receiving role, purpose, caveat, decision owner, and unresolved authority—not an unsupported acronym-based claim of permission.
title: Fusion Centers and Task Forces: Specify the Coordination Model

raw: 2.9 Intelligence Oversight: Congressional, Judicial, Executive Mechanisms
teaching_note: In U.S. orientation, congressional committees perform legislative scrutiny and funding/authorization functions; courts address matters within their legal jurisdiction; executive oversight includes agency review, inspectors general, and privacy/civil-liberties mechanisms. These are different checks, not three interchangeable sign-off routes, and inspectors general are not courts. The public overview is an introductory snapshot inspected on 6 November 2026, not a legal opinion about a particular activity; verify dated governing records before assigning a specific approval duty [@official_intelligence_gov_how_ic_works]. In the synthetic port case, an analytic reviewer checks support, a release reviewer checks permitted distribution, and an oversight/legal role receives the unresolved authority issue; none may cure it merely by endorsing the conclusion.
title: Oversight: Legislative, Judicial, and Executive Functions
